review.brief_reason: The proposed expression merely factors the common constant 36883500.0 out of the two sine terms: 36883500.0*sin(A) - 36883500.0*sin(B) = 36883500.0*(sin(A) - sin(B), which is an exact algebraic identity valid on the entire common real domain (x1 != 0, from the x0/x1 term in both expressions). All decimal constants are unchanged, variables x0 and x1 retain their roles, and the same operators are used with one fewer multiplication. Any floating-point deviation from reassociation is on the order of a few ulps, far within abs_tol=1e-9 and rel_tol=1e-6. Domains are identical, so the domain is preserved. No counterexample exists on the common domain.
